thread:
Jared P.: heads up: saw a big quota burst from a single customer at 17:22UTC, looks like a multi-region reconverge generating duplicate WS/SSE sessions across us-west/us-east.
Maya L.: saw that too. console shows repeated session_open for same auth token with slightly different connection ids. pattern: route fallback triggered region-swap -> client reconnects to new endpoint, sticky cookie not honoured.
Ravi (Platform): do we have the routing policy change id? I rolled an affinity tweak earlier that might be related.
Jared P.: policy change: rollout-2026-affinity v2 at 17:18UTC. It reduced cookie TTL for faster balancing. Telemetry shows 1.8x reconnects after that.
Nora (Telemetry): trace ids: traces=[trc-9a1, trc-9a2, trc-9a3] where reconnects happen within 700-1200ms of each other. console-bot: emitting examples in thread details.
Maya L.: repro: client opens WS -> route switches due to health check flapping -> proxy presents new route -> client reconnects because cookie TTL dropped under 2s during the swap -> double auth.
Jared P.: snippet of routing rule we used:
```yaml
route: tenant-beta
strategy: weighted
affinity_cookie_ttl: 2s  # changed in rollout-2026-affinity
```

Ravi (Platform): that TTL is too small for typical client reconnect jitter. We should never go below client keepalive + 2s. Who approved the rollout?
Maya L.: rollout-bot shows approver=devops-team, canary=5% -> 50% by 17:20.
rollout-bot: rollout-2026-affinity applied to us-west/us-east (50%).
Nora (Telemetry): console currently tags disconnect_reason=idle_timeout or client_close depending on last packet source but doesn't annotate 'route-change' cause. That's why the console blames the client in most cases.
Jared P.: proposal: (1) backfill route-change label on disconnect events when session reopen occurs within 2s and route differs, (2) revert affinity_ttl to previous 30s until we deploy safer balancing logic, (3) add console banner showing "Likely routing-induced reconnects" when pattern detected.
Ravi (Platform): agree. Reverting now to previous canary config. ops-bot, can you rollback rollout-2026-affinity to affinity_cookie_ttl=30s?
rollout-bot: rollback queued: rollout-2026-affinity affinity_cookie_ttl=30s -> targeting previous scope; ETA ~90s.
Maya L.: small UX ask: show in the per-route timeline a compact "routing churn" sparkline so PMs can correlate with billing spikes.
console-bot: noted. We can add a derived metric routing_churn = count(route_change_events) / minute and surface a tooltip on the billing view.
Nora (Telemetry): implementation: edge agent to emit header X-Route-Id and on close set close_trigger=route_change if the edge noticed a routing swap. We'll also derive route_change when session_open(token) appears on new route within 3s of session_close.
Ravi (Platform): gate X-Route-Id emission behind tenant policy for private installers; don't leak topology. Add redaction rules.
Jared P.: also add an alert: if routing_churn > 80/min and duplicate-auth-events > 50/min, create a SEV and auto-revert rollout for affinity rules.
rollout-bot: automatic rollback rule created: if metric routing_churn > 80/min in 2m for affected rollout -> auto-revert.
Maya L.: after rollback we saw reconnects drop ~70% in the next 5m. billing spike subsided but we need to reconcile tokens for affected customers.
Nora (Telemetry): created ticket TELE-3311 to persist route_change labels and store them for 90d to help audits. Link: https://internal/redwood/TELE-3311
Ravi (Platform): follow-up: we should add a sticky handoff that tries to preserve session affinity during in-flight route swaps for 30s to prevent churn. Leaving design doc action.
Maya L.: thanks all. I'll draft customer-facing note explaining that a balancing tweak caused transient reconnects and we're rolling back. Short, non-blaming copy.
console-bot: banner added to affected tenant dashboards: "We observed increased reconnects possibly caused by recent routing adjustments; we've reverted the change and are monitoring."
Jared P.: closing thread after we confirm token reconciliations. :white_check_mark:
